start_chart_desc: Overhead chart of bright reference stars. North is up and east is left. Stars are shown as position guides in daylight.
start_eyebrow: Your window into the night sky
start_title: Find your place among the stars.
start_intro: Choose a place and time, look around the sky, then select an object to learn what you are seeing. Real catalog stars and calculated planet positions bring each view to life.
start_data: The star catalog is included for offline use. NOAA aurora forecasts are optional and need an internet connection.
start_day: Daylight · star positions shown as guides
obs_aurora_forecast_geometry: NOAA model guides this illustrative curtain toward
obs_aurora_forecast_cell: is the sampled poleward grid estimate; height, shape and colour are simulated.
obs_aurora_forecast_below: This sampled NOAA forecast produces no curtain above this simulated horizon. Actual viewing also depends on darkness, clouds and local conditions.
obs_noaa_idle: Fetch a current forecast, then apply it to the live sky.
obs_noaa_retry: NOAA forecast unavailable. Try fetching again; the simulated sky is still available.
obs_noaa_location_changed: The saved forecast was sampled for a different location. Fetch again for this site.
obs_noaa_poleward_grid: strongest poleward cell on this longitude
obs_noaa_provenance: A model driven by space-weather observations, usually 30–90 minutes ahead. Values sample a 1° grid; they do not include your clouds, light pollution or obstructions. Curtain height, colour and motion are illustrative.
obs_accuracy_limits: HYG catalog coordinates are adjusted for Earth's changing axis direction. Sun, Moon and planet positions are classroom approximations computed for your time and location. Lunar parallax is not modeled; near-horizon positions and rise/set times are approximate. Refraction assumes a standard atmosphere, and sky darkness is a chosen setting, not measured local weather.
obs_visual_limits: The Moon uses NASA LRO surface imagery. Landscapes and Milky Way detail are illustrative; they are not images of the selected site. Meteors and aurora are simulations. Deep-time star motion is an extrapolation.
obs_noaa_current_sky_only: Forecast data applies to the current sky. Use Live now, pause time-lapse and reset deep time to apply it.
obs_coordinate_error: Enter a number in this range; the sky keeps the last valid position.
obs_clock_error: Choose a valid date (1900–2099) and local time. Some times are skipped when daylight saving begins. The sky keeps the last valid time.
obs_search_centered: Centered and selected in the sky.
obs_search_details_only: Object details selected. The camera stayed in place.
obs_search_return_present: Return to the present-day sky to find this object.
obs_catalog_loading_full: Loading the full star catalog. Bright stars remain available.
obs_catalog_fallback_retry: The full star catalog could not load. Showing built-in bright stars.
obs_search_help: Search catalog stars, planets, the Sun, Moon, and deep-sky objects. Enter opens the first result. Objects hidden from this sky still have details.
obs_search_empty: No matches in the loaded catalog. Try a common name, HIP number, or Messier number.
skymap_fixed_moment: Time set in Observatory. Offsets start from this moment:
obs_map_pause: Pause time-lapse to carry this moment to the sky map.
obs_map_today: Return deep time to Today to open the sky map.
obs_open_skymap: Open this place and time in the Sky Map
obs_selection_faint: Hidden by daylight or sky brightness
obs_accuracy_limits_topocentric: Star coordinates account for Earth's changing axis direction. Moon positions include the shift caused by your location on Earth (parallax), checked against NASA/JPL reference positions. Sun, Moon and planet positions remain classroom approximations for a sea-level observer. Refraction assumes a standard atmosphere; terrain and local weather are not modeled. Sky darkness is a chosen setting.
obs_zone_out_of_range: This moment is outside 1900–2099 in that time zone. Choose a date further inside the supported range first.
